plan: Given my value of $10, I need to consider the optimal bidding strategy in a second-price auction with two other rational bidders. A common strategy in such auctions is to bid your true value, as this is a dominant strategy that maximizes your expected profit regardless of what other bidders do. I will bid my true value to ensure I win when my value is higher than the second-highest bid, and I pay no more than my value.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with payment equal to the second-highest bid (Vickrey auction variant). My goal is to maximize profit. In a Vickrey auction, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. This is a dominant strategy because bidding below my value risks losing a profitable item, and bidding above my value risks winning an item at a loss. Since my value is $30, I will bid $30.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with private values. Since I only have one round, I will try to maximize my profit for this specific round. My value is $25. I will bid slightly above my value to secure the win, assuming other bidders will bid around their values. I aim to win at a price as close to my value as possible. I will bid $25.1 to ensure I win if others bid their value.
